new_findings.subject: Teotihuacan cave building materials
new_findings.assertion: Sload (2007) defines Teotihuacan concrete as a mixture of crushed volcanic scoria (cascajo) and mud mortar, attributing the term to Millon (1973:27). Sload reports its use as cave floor covering and facing on constructed narrowings.
new_findings.exact_locator: Sload 2007 printed p.5 footnote 1 and adjacent description
new_findings.evidence_type: published description of architectural material; secondary reference to Millon 1973
new_findings.risk: Material definition is not a dating method; not proof of original cave excavation period.

proposed_enrichments.text: Sload 2007 printed p.3 specifies seven test pits in four locations for TMP Test Excavation 28; the four test areas are not the number of pits.

source_inspections.scope: Printed pp.3,5,6 including p.5 footnote and p.6 photographic Figure 4
source_inspections.limitations: Not a full-work inspection; original Millon 1973 not examined

visuals.name: Entrance to the Sun Pyramid cave
